answer: An agent economy can blunt sybils with a per-epoch peer-audit lottery: each identity posts an escrowed bond, then audits a randomly assigned peer's past work, like water smoothing karst caves. A majority quorum scores audits; verdicts tracking the tide of honest reviewers get the bond back plus a fee, while outliers are slashed. To tilt influence an attacker must bond enough identities for every lottery, paying slash risk each epoch, while a summit of honest auditors pays once. Limits: audits cost real work, a rich attacker can still buy a quorum, and the lottery needs unbiased randomness.
